summary:
VERIFIED BASELINE (all commands run by me; nothing in the project root was modified, and the real backend/data/mirror.duckdb and .wal mtimes are unchanged).

PASSING
- Backend tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` gives `22 passed, 1 warning in 9.16s` on Python 3.14.5. The same 22 also pass on 3.12, on 3.11.9 with pandas 3.0.6, and on 3.11.9 with pandas 2.3.3 and numpy 2.2.6. `python -X dev -m pytest -W error` (ignoring only the Starlette httpx deprecation) gives `22 passed`, so there are no ResourceWarning or DeprecationWarning problems on 3.14.
- Tests are hermetic today: tests/conftest.py:7-11 redirects MIRROR_DB_PATH, DEMO_PASSWORD, MIRROR_JWT_SECRET and MIRROR_WEB_DIST into a temp dir. There is no caveat on the real DB: its mtimes before and after are identical (DB 20:04:41, WAL 20:10:55).
- Web: `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exits 0 with no output. `vite build` to the scratchpad exits 0 with no warnings: 23 modules, JS 247.34 kB (77.29 kB gzip), CSS 10.89 kB. A fresh `npm ci` followed by `npm run build` (the Dockerfile web stage, `tsc -b && vite build`) also exits 0 with the identical bundle hashes, and `npm audit` reports "found 0 vulnerabilities".
- Pins: every pin resolves. PyPI has fastapi 0.142.2, uvicorn 0.46.0, duckdb 1.5.6, pydantic 2.13.3, PyJWT 2.12.1, PyYAML 6.0.3, httpx 0.28.1 and pytest 9.1.1. npm has react 19.3.0, vite 8.3.1, typescript 7.0.2, plugin-react 6.1.1 and @types 19.3.0; package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) is consistent and `pip check` says "No broken requirements found." Linux cp312 wheels exist for every dependency, including duckdb, pyarrow, numpy, pandas and uvloop, so the `python:3.12-slim` build is resolvable. The pins also resolve for CPython 3.10 (numpy 2.2.6, pandas 2.3.3). Both Docker base tags exist (`docker manifest inspect` for python:3.12-slim and node:22-slim).
- Python 3.14 compatibility: no failures. grep found no utcnow, get_event_loop, pydantic v1 APIs or on_event, and no 3.11+ only syntax.
- Production-mode smoke on my own scratch DB and port 8765 (now stopped): static serving works (/ 200, hashed js and css 200), /api/docs and /api/openapi.json return 404, and the CSP header is present. In a browser, login, the twin (82% home, 55% family), and the NL switch (`PUT /api/me/preferences` 200) all work. There were zero securitypolicyviolation events and no console errors, and the bundle contains no external URLs, @import or eval.
- Measured: `generate(100000)` takes 25.0 s and writes 6,116,388 events and 5,436 planted moments, matching the README's "~25 s" and "6.1M". Peak working set is 970 MiB and peak commit is 1,994 MiB.
- Live stack: backend PID 35448 on 127.0.0.1:8000 answers `/api/health` 200 (started 20:07); Vite dev PID 32592 on ::1:5173 answers 200 on localhost.

NOT VERIFIED
- The live DB content, because it is exclusively locked by the running server (copy fails with "Device or resource busy").
- A real `docker build` (I did not pull about 400 MB of base images).
- gcloud upload rules (gcloud is not installed).
- Python 3.10 execution (not installed).

Findings follow, ordered by severity. They include one process incident I caused in the shared scratchpad, reported honestly in the last finding.

findings.title: Live demo database state is unknown and cannot be inspected while the server runs; it has been written to since generation
findings.detail: The task's copy step failed: both mirror.duckdb and mirror.duckdb.wal are exclusively locked by the running backend (PID 35448, started 20:07:34), so I could not query the demo DB. What is known: the DB file was written at 20:04:41 by the generator, but the 14,424,154-byte WAL is dated 20:10:55, after the server started. So something wrote after generation: a full run (engine.py:98-99 does CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE signal_hits and twin), feedback (api.py:230), consent changes (api.py:249), language changes (api.py:264), or a custom moment (engine.py:70). All of these persist across restarts. The demo script depends on a clean state: sofie's 'growing family' must not already be rejected (README.md:103), the electric-car moment must not already exist (README.md:106, stored in custom_moments), and languages must be EN. I cannot confirm any of that. Other agents are also exercising servers, so the real DB on port 8000 could be polluted if any of them point at it. generate.py:317-320 deletes the DB and WAL before rebuilding; on Windows that unlink raises PermissionError if the server is still running, so the server must be stopped first.
findings.evidence:
$ cp backend/data/mirror.duckdb scratchpad/dbcopy/ -> cp: cannot open '.../backend/data/mirror.duckdb' for reading: Device or resource busy
.NET FileShare.ReadWrite|Delete open -> 'The process cannot access the file ... because it is being used by another process.'
ls --time-style=full-iso backend/data: mirror.duckdb 32256000 2026-09-30 20:04:41 ; mirror.duckdb.wal 14424154 2026-09-30 20:10:55
CommandLine of PID 35448/54084: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m uvicorn mirror.api:app --port 8000 (CreationDate 20:07:34)
findings.fix: Immediately before the demo: stop the API on 8000, run `cd backend && .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m mirror.generate --customers 100000` (25.0 s measured), restart uvicorn, then log in as sofie, marc, an, jan and po once to confirm the README table. Keep other agents and tests off port 8000 after that.
findings.demo_impact: If feedback or the EV moment was already applied, the 0:50 and 2:15 beats of the script silently fail or look pre-baked.

reasons:
The core observation holds but is an operational pre-demo checklist item, not a code defect. Severity high and several supporting claims are wrong.

CONFIRMED (reproduced):
- cp of mirror.duckdb and mirror.duckdb.wal fails with "Device or resource busy". Port 8000 is owned by PID 35448, started 20:07:34 from the user's VS Code pwsh (PID 54364).
- Main file is 32,256,000 bytes, last written 20:04:41. WAL is 14,424,154 bytes, last written 20:10:55. Both were unchanged when I rechecked at 21:17.
- A fresh `generate --customers 100000` in scratchpad gives a main file of exactly 32,256,000 bytes (16.7 s). The live main file has never been checkpointed, so every post-generation write sits in the WAL.

"Written since generation" is partly expected, not suspicious by itself:
- generate.py:363-372 creates no twin or signal_hits tables. So the first server start always runs `run_population()` (engine.py:38-39) and `sync_runtime()` (engine.py:52).
- In my scratch replication that startup alone leaves a WAL of about 7.12 MB. The reviewer did not account for this.

WAL forensics on scratch copies of a fresh 100k DB, compared with the live 14,424,154 bytes:

| Sequence | WAL size |
|---|---|
| Startup plus one extra full run (`POST /api/po/run`, engine.py:91-104) | 14,240,470 |
| Startup, add EV moment, extra full run | 14,896,824 |
| Startup, two extra runs | checkpoints; WAL resets to about 2 MB |

- Per-action cost: one feedback or `refresh_customer` is about 20 KB, a guidance render about 0.8 KB, a language change about 0.1 KB.
- So the live DB most likely saw one extra PO run plus roughly 9 small customer-level writes (feedback or consent), probably a rehearsal.
- An EV add-and-run is excluded, because it would leave at least 14.90 MB and a WAL never shrinks without a checkpoint.
- Exactly which customer writes happened cannot be determined while the file is locked. The user's VS Code uvicorn log would show it.

REFUTED or OVERSTATED:
1. "Other agents could pollute port 8000": the WAL has not changed since 20:10:55, before this investigation started (20:16). Other agents ran servers on other ports. scratchpad/backend.log shows 127.0.0.1:8001, and they used their own DB copies. tests/conftest.py:8 points the tests at a temp DB.
2. "The demo beats silently fail": they are visible and fixable in one click.
   - A pre-existing feedback shows an Undo button (web/src/views/Mirror.tsx:181-184, posting status "clear" handled at api.py:225-227).
   - A pre-existing EV moment returns a visible 409 "already exists" (engine.py:65-66, api.py:417-418, shown at ProductOwner.tsx:56), and a Remove button deletes it (ProductOwner.tsx:190-194).
   - Language is a one-click EN/NL/FR switch (Mirror.tsx:56-66).
3. "generate.py:317-320 raises PermissionError on Windows if the server is running": false on this machine (duckdb 1.5.6, same venv). Tested with one process holding the DB open and another unlinking the DB and WAL and regenerating at the same path:
   - Both unlinks succeed and the new file is created.
   - The running process keeps seeing the OLD data, while a fresh process sees the new data.
   - The failure mode is therefore silent, not loud. Regenerating without stopping the API leaves the live server on the polluted DB until restart.
   - README.md:74 already says to stop the API first, which is the right procedure.
4. The reset is already documented (README.md:74), quick (about 17-25 s), and needs no code change.

Recommendation: keep "stop the API, regenerate, restart, then log in as sofie, marc, an, jan and po" as a pre-demo step.

VALID, but overstated at "high", and one supporting claim is wrong.

1. Cannot inspect the live DB (reproduced). `cp backend/data/mirror.duckdb` fails with "Device or resource busy" while PID 35448 (uvicorn, started 20:07:34) holds it. The live files are unchanged after ~30 min: DB 32,256,000 B at 20:04:41, WAL 14,424,154 B at 20:10:55. Nothing has touched them since, including my scratch work. Tests cannot hit it (tests/conftest.py:8 sets MIRROR_DB_PATH to a temp dir before any mirror import).

2. The live DB has been exercised since generation, which is stronger than the reviewer's inference. A WAL mtime after server start proves little, because startup itself writes. generate.py creates no twin/signal_hits/moments_rt, so engine.py:36-39 runs run_population on first start. I measured this on a scratch 100k DB built with the same generator:
- Startup alone gives WAL = 7,120,779 B (A).
- Startup plus the first /api/me/guidance call adds about 770 B of message_cache rows (B, 7,121,554).
- Startup plus one POST /api/po/run ("Run on all customers", the 0:20 beat) gives 14,241,258 B (C). A repeat gave 14,241,274, so the sizes are deterministic.
- Adding the EV moment and running gives 14,897,642 B (D), which is already larger than the live WAL.
- Each customer-side write that calls refresh_customer (feedback or consent, api.py:234/252) adds about 20 KB.
- Startup + guidance + 1 run + 9 feedback refreshes gives 14,424,913 B (I), against live 14,424,154, a gap of 759 B (0.005%).
- The live DB file is still 32,256,000 B, the same as a fresh generation, so no checkpoint has happened and the WAL holds everything since generation.
Conclusion: the live DB was almost certainly used after startup, with one full run plus roughly 9 per-customer writes. The EV moment plus a run did not happen (D is too big). The net state, meaning whether sofie's feedback is left rejected or cleared, cannot be determined without the lock.

3. Demo impact is overstated: the failures are visible and fixable in one click, not silent.
- Already-rejected growing_family shows as a "rejected" card with a note and an Undo button (web/src/views/Mirror.tsx:134,177,181-184), which calls feedback "clear" (api.py:225-227).
- An existing ev_purchase makes the "Validate & go live" button fail visibly. Engine.add_custom raises ValueError (engine.py:65-66), the API returns 409 (api.py:417-418), and ProductOwner.tsx:56 shows a red error. The moment also appears in the Moments table with a "new" tag and a Remove button (ProductOwner.tsx:179,190-194), which deletes it and re-runs.
- The finding also missed that buying_home must not already be confirmed for the "ask, then she says yes" beat. A clean scratch DB matches the README: sofie buying_home 0.82 ask and growing_family 0.545 ask, language en.

4. One claim in the finding is false. generate.py:317-320 does NOT raise PermissionError on Windows while the server runs. In scratch I started uvicorn on a copy, then ran `mirror.generate --customers 100` against the same path. It exited 0 and replaced the file (32,256,000 B to 1,585,152 B). The running server kept serving the old data (signal-kinds event sum 6,116,388 before and after generate) and showed 5,977 only after a restart. So regenerating without stopping the API looks successful but leaves the demo on the old dirty state. The recommended fix (stop API, regenerate, restart, log in as sofie/marc/an/jan/po to confirm) is correct and documented at README.md:74, and takes under a minute (my generate runs took 15-20 s). The real trap is forgetting the stop and restart, and the finding should say that instead.

Net: a real pre-demo hygiene risk on a DB that is probably not pristine, but it is a checklist item with a documented one-minute reset and visible in-UI recovery, not a code defect. Medium.

findings.title: No Gemini, Vertex or ElevenLabs key is configured, so Listen shows an error and all intros are templates
findings.detail: config.py:62-70 reads GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY from the environment or .env. I printed only booleans through the app's own loader (the .env contents were never displayed): all three are False. In my production-bundle browser run, pressing the Listen button after switching to NL produced the message 'Voice channel not configured (set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)', in English even with the NL UI, and it names an env var. README.md:104 has the presenter do exactly 'Switch to NL, press Listen', and README.md:142 admits the Gemini and ElevenLabs paths were never tested with real keys. Caveat: the running server on 8000 could have keys in its own process environment, which I cannot see.
findings.evidence:
python (conftest-style pop + config import): ENV: dev | GEMINI set: False | VERTEX project set: False | ELEVENLABS set: False
Browser (prod bundle, NL active): afterListen voiceMsg -> "Voice channel not configured (set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)"
API: POST /api/me/guidance/buying_home/voice returns 503 without a key (asserted at tests/test_security.py:176)
findings.fix: Put ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (and GEMINI_API_KEY) in .env and restart the API, then dry-run the Listen click in NL and EN at least twice before the demo. See the next finding: adding keys will break the test suite unless conftest is fixed.
findings.demo_impact: The voice channel is a headline wow moment; without a key the audience sees an error string at the climax of the customer segment, and the 'AI writes the words' claim shows template text.

reasons:
I could not refute the mechanics, but this is a documented graceful degradation plus a config and demo-prep gap, not a code defect, so I rate it medium rather than high.

Confirmed by reading the code:
- With no key, config.py:62-70 leaves the Gemini, Vertex and ElevenLabs settings empty. channels.py:70 makes _gemini() return None, so channels.py:141-143 uses the template text and stores source "template". channels.py:104-105 makes tts() return None.
- api.py:316-317 then raises HTTPException(503, "Voice channel not configured (set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)"). The string is hard-coded English, so it is shown unlocalised under the NL UI and names an env var.
- web/src/api.ts:38 copies the server's detail into ApiError. Mirror.tsx:226-227 stores it and Mirror.tsx:270 renders it as small muted text under the card.
- No fallback exists. A grep of web/src found no speechSynthesis, no audio element and no .mp3, and the repo contains no audio files.
- README.md:104 scripts "press Listen" as a demo step. README.md:142 admits the Gemini and ElevenLabs paths were never tested with real keys. tests/test_security.py:176 asserts the 503 without a key.

Why I rate it medium:
- README.md:71-72 already documents the behaviour: "Without them everything works with templates, and the Listen button says voice isn't configured." It is intended degradation.
- Nothing crashes. The decisions, confidence bars, advisor view and product-owner console all work without any key. Only the Listen button and the claim that AI writes the intros are affected.
- Skipping Listen, or adding a key, avoids it.

Key state: I did not read or print .env, so I cannot confirm the keys are empty myself. Evidence consistent with "no keys":
- My shell has no GEMINI, ELEVENLABS or GOOGLE_CLOUD variables set.
- .env was last modified at 19:53:58, before the server on port 8000 (PID 35448) started at 20:07:34, so it loaded the current file.
- A copy of the live DB made earlier in the session (scratchpad/db/replica.duckdb, which I copied and queried) has message_cache rows only with source "template" (7 rows) and none with "llm", including Sofie's buying_home and growing_family rows.
- A process-level env var on the server (the reviewer's caveat) remains unverifiable. I could not copy the live DB because it is locked.

Improvement: hide or disable Listen when voice is unavailable, or fall back to browser speech synthesis. Add a localised message instead of the raw 503 detail that names an env var. If the team has keys, put them in .env, restart, and dry-run Listen in NL and EN twice before presenting.

Relevant files: backend/mirror/config.py:62-70, backend/mirror/channels.py:70,103-113,141-143, backend/mirror/api.py:302-318, web/src/views/Mirror.tsx:213-229,266-270, web/src/api.ts:34-46, README.md:71-72,104,142.

Reproduced: the facts are right, but this is a config gap rather than a code defect, and it has a documented fallback, so I rate it medium rather than high.

**Keys are unset (what I ran).** I ran a scratch script (scratchpad/refute_keys/cfg.py) that imports the app's own config loader and prints booleans only; .env was never read or printed.
- The process env before the loader has GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY all False.
- After the loader (env plus .env), all three are still False, with ENV=dev.
- Windows User and Machine env vars for all three are also unset.
- `channels.tts("x")` returns None and `channels._gemini("nl", {...})` returns None.
- A grep showed the .env key lines (backend/.env-style entries at .env:15, 17, 22) as empty assignments, matching .env.example.

**Error path (code read).**
- config.py:62-70 reads the three keys from the environment.
- channels.py:104 makes `tts()` return None when `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` is empty.
- api.py:316-317 turns that into `HTTPException(503, "Voice channel not configured (set ELEVENLABS_API_KEY)")`. The string is hard-coded in English and names the env var.
- web/src/api.ts:38 copies `detail` into `ApiError.message`.
- web/src/views/Mirror.tsx:226-227 and 270 render that message as plain text under the card, with no localisation.
- tests/test_security.py:176 asserts this 503.

**Intros are templates.** channels.py:141-144 falls back to `TEMPLATES` with `source="template"` whenever `_gemini` returns None. The only message_cache copy I could open was a scratchpad replica (scratchpad/db/replica.duckdb), which held 7 rows, all `source='template'` (2 en, 5 nl). The live mirror.duckdb is locked by the server, so I could not query it.

**README already says this.**
- README:71-72 says the keys are optional and that Listen "says voice isn't configured".
- README:142 admits the Gemini and ElevenLabs paths have never been tested with real keys.
- README:104 does put "Switch to NL, press Listen" in the demo script, so the error would show at a scripted step.

**Why medium, not high.**
- The error is a designed, tested fallback with a config-only fix (add ELEVENLABS_API_KEY and restart), not a bug.
- Templates are valid, working output, and the UI only shows the "AI written" note when `written_by == "llm"` (Mirror.tsx:271). Nothing in the UI claims AI wrote a template.
- Two things are still real. A raw English string naming an env var would be shown to judges under an NL UI. Listen has no graceful degradation (no hidden button, no browser speech-synthesis fallback). That justifies medium. It becomes high only if the presenter still clicks Listen with no key.

**Caveats.**
- I could not see the environment of the server on 8000 (pid 35448). `/api/health` returns only `{"ok":true}`, and its command line is plain `python -m uvicorn mirror.api:app --port 8000`. Since .env and the User and Machine env are empty, it almost certainly has no keys, but that is an inference.
- I did not call the live server, because every `/api/me/guidance` call writes to message_cache.

**Extra points for the suggested fix.**
- Adding GEMINI_API_KEY will not change intros already cached. `Channels.intro` (channels.py:128-131) returns any cached row regardless of `source`, and nothing ever deletes from message_cache (only channels.py:122 and 146 and the db.py:82 schema touch it). Cached template rows for sofie and lucas would stay templates until the DB is regenerated or those rows are deleted.
- The reviewer's follow-on claim about the test suite also holds. conftest.py:12-14 pops the three env vars, but `config._load_dotenv` (config.py:30) re-adds them from .env on import. With keys in .env, `test_voice_only_for_own_active_guidance` (test_security.py:176) would no longer see 503.

findings.title: Test suite is not isolated from .env: keys popped in conftest are re-loaded from .env on import
findings.detail: conftest.py:12-14 pops GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY, then line 18 imports mirror.generate, which imports config. config.py:26 loads .env with `key not in os.environ`, so every popped key is repopulated from the .env file. Today it is harmless because .env has none of them. But README.md:71 tells the user to add exactly these keys to .env, after which test_guidance_falls_back_to_templates_without_ai (tests/test_engine.py:30-33, expects written_by == 'template') and test_voice_only_for_own_active_guidance (tests/test_security.py:176, expects 503) will fail, and the run would make real, billed Gemini and ElevenLabs calls. I reproduced the mechanism offline in a scratch replica of config.py with a fake .env (no network); the fix also works in that replica.
findings.evidence:
replica: after conftest-style pop + `from mirror import config` -> GEMINI_API_KEY re-populated from .env after conftest pop: True ; ELEVENLABS_API_KEY re-populated from .env after conftest pop: True
with proposed fix (os.environ[k] = "" instead of pop): GEMINI set: False | ELEVENLABS set: False
findings.fix: In conftest.py replace `os.environ.pop(k, None)` with `os.environ[k] = ""` for the three keys (config.py:26 skips keys already present, and config.py:62-68 treat empty as unset). Do this before adding real keys for the demo.
findings.demo_impact: Indirect: a red or paid test run the night before the demo when keys are added.

reasons:
The mechanism is real and I reproduced it with the project's own code, but it is latent and only affects tests, so I rate it low rather than medium.

Code path, read directly:
- backend/tests/conftest.py:12-14 use os.environ.pop for GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY. conftest.py:18 then imports mirror.generate, which does `from . import config` (generate.py:23).
- backend/mirror/config.py:26 loads .env with `key not in os.environ`. A popped key is absent, so a non-empty value in .env is put straight back. conftest.py:8-11 only protect the four variables it sets, not these three.
- I found no other guard: no pytest.ini, setup.cfg, tox.ini or pyproject, and conftest.py is the only conftest.

Reproduction, in a scratch copy of backend/mirror, tests and moments with a FAKE .env (GEMINI_API_KEY=fake, ELEVENLABS_API_KEY=fake) and the network blocked by a dead HTTPS_PROXY. I did not read the real .env. It exists (1091 bytes) and I only checked that it exists.
- With conftest as shipped, a probe test printed `config.GEMINI_API_KEY` and `config.ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` as set (True/True).
- In that same run, tests/test_security.py:176 (test_voice_only_for_own_active_guidance) failed with `assert 502 == 503`. The log showed "TTS failed: ConnectError", so the keys from .env were used. With a valid key the same call would be a real billed ElevenLabs request returning 200, which fails the test just the same.
- After replacing the pops with `os.environ[k] = ""` (the proposed fix), the probe printed False/False and the full suite gave 23 passed.
- The fix holds because config.py:26 sees the key as present and skips it, and config.py:62-68 turn an empty string into "".

Why it is test-only and low severity:
- The Gemini half of the finding is correct in principle but I did not exercise it. With a valid GEMINI_API_KEY and network, `_gemini` (channels.py:15-46) would succeed and `intro()` would store source "llm" (channels.py:22), so test_guidance_falls_back_to_templates_without_ai (tests/test_engine.py:30-33) would fail on `written_by == "template"`. With an invalid key or no network it silently falls back to templates and passes.
- The billing exposure is a handful of Gemini calls plus one ElevenLabs call per test run.
- README.md:71-72 only say the keys are optional env settings. They do not literally say ".env", but config.py:1 and .env.example:15,22 make .env the obvious place.
- The demo app does not run pytest and is not affected. The only consequence is a confusing red or paid `pytest` run after real keys are added, so the fix is cheap hygiene to apply before adding keys.

The mechanism is real, but it is a test-hygiene issue with no effect on the running demo, so low rather than medium.

**Code read.**
- backend/tests/conftest.py:12-14 pops GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT and ELEVENLABS_API_KEY.
- Line 18 imports mirror.generate, which does `from . import config` (generate.py:23).
- config.py:15-30 runs `_load_dotenv()` at import. It reads REPO_DIR/.env and sets a key when `key and value and key not in os.environ` (config.py:26). A popped key is absent, so it is repopulated from .env.
- Nothing in conftest imports `mirror` before the pops, and the only other test files are test_engine.py and test_security.py. No pytest.ini or other conftest in backend/ matters.

**Reproduced, offline.**
- I copied backend/mirror, moments, examples and tests into the scratchpad with a fake .env containing fake keys. The real .env was never read.
- A conftest-style pop followed by `import mirror.config` gave GEMINI, GCP and ELEVEN all set (True). Replacing the pops with `os.environ[k] = ""` gave all False.
- I ran the two named tests in the replica with httpx.post stubbed, so there was no network. Both fail as the reviewer predicted:
  - test_engine.py:32 (`written_by == "template"`) fails.
  - test_security.py:176 gets 200 instead of 503.
  - The stub recorded 3 Gemini calls and 1 ElevenLabs call, which would have been real and billed.
- With the proposed one-line fix applied to the replica conftest only, the full suite passed: 22 passed, 0 outbound calls. The real project files are unchanged (conftest.py:12-14 still use pop).

**Unverified.** I did not read the real .env, as instructed, so the reviewer's statement that it holds none of these keys is unconfirmed. README.md:71-72 does tell the user to add exactly these keys.

**Severity.**
- Tests are not part of the live 3-minute demo, and the app itself is unaffected.
- The tests use a temp DB (conftest.py:8, set before config import), so `message_cache` in the real mirror.duckdb is not polluted.
- The spend is a handful of calls per run, in my replica 3 Gemini and 1 ElevenLabs.
- The only demo-relevant risk is a red or slightly billed test run after keys are added; run the suite before adding keys, or apply the fix.
- The fix is correct: `os.environ[k] = ""` works because config.py:26 skips keys already present and config.py:62-68 treat an empty value as unset.

- I could not confirm this. `gcloud` is not installed, and the docs I fetched (gcloudignore topic, Cloud Run source-deploy page) do not spell it out. The problem is therefore certain for a plain `docker build` and uncertain for the README's gcloud command.
- I also could not reproduce a real `docker build`: the Docker Desktop engine is not running (`docker info` failed to reach the daemon).

- Nothing breaks: `pip install` and `uvicorn` do not touch the copied `.venv`. The cost is a build context of about 300 MB and an image several hundred MB larger, so a slower deploy or upload, and only if Docker or Cloud Run is used at all.
- The `backend/.env` point is hypothetical. No such file exists.
- The suggested fix (add `**/.venv`, `**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, `**/*.duckdb`, `**/*.duckdb.wal`, `**/*.tsbuildinfo` to `.dockerignore`) is sound. It is a one-line cleanup and not worth risking before the demo.

findings.title: Cloud Run deploy command leaves the demo stateful and slow: per-instance DB regenerated on every cold start, tight 2 Gi memory
findings.detail: README.md:79-80 deploys with `--memory 2Gi` and no --min-instances or --max-instances. The Dockerfile CMD (Dockerfile:20) regenerates the synthetic DB whenever data/mirror.duckdb is missing, before uvicorn binds the port. On this dev machine that takes 25.0 s (measured 6,116,388 events) with a 970 MiB peak working set and a 1,994 MiB peak commit, against a 2 Gi limit, so headroom is about 2x before the server's own tables (engine.py:98-99) and writes are added. Because the container filesystem is ephemeral and each instance has its own DuckDB, (a) every cold start loses sofie's feedback and the EV moment, and (b) with more than one instance the customer and advisor views can disagree (feedback written on instance A, advisor served by B), which would contradict the 'gone everywhere' claim. The README already admits rate limiting is per-process. Also the Cloud Run path has never been run here (no gcloud; I did not run docker build).
findings.evidence:
baseline_gen_mem.py: stats: {'customers': 100000, 'events': 6116388, 'planted_moments': 5436, 'advisors': 50, 'seconds': 25.0} | wall seconds: 25.2 | peak working set MiB: 970; peak commit MiB: 1994
Dockerfile:20: CMD ["sh","-c","[ -f data/mirror.duckdb ] || python -m mirror.generate --customers ${MIRROR_CUSTOMERS:-100000}; exec uvicorn ..."]
findings.fix: If the cloud URL will be shown: deploy with `--min-instances 1 --max-instances 1 --cpu 2 --no-cpu-throttling --memory 4Gi`, warm it with one login before presenting, and do not redeploy after the rehearsal. Otherwise demo locally and treat Cloud Run as a backup only.
findings.demo_impact: A cold-start delay of 30 s or more, a reset demo state, or inconsistent customer and advisor views if the cloud URL is used live.

reasons:
Partly valid, but overstated. Severity is low unless the live demo runs from the cloud URL.

CONFIRMED (code read and commands run):
- README.md:79-80 deploys with `--memory 2Gi` and no `--min-instances`, `--max-instances` or `--cpu`.
- Dockerfile:20 runs `python -m mirror.generate` whenever `data/mirror.duckdb` is missing, before `exec uvicorn`.
- `.dockerignore` excludes `backend/data`, so the image never contains a DB and every cold start regenerates it.
- I reproduced the generation in the scratchpad with `venv312` (Python 3.12, as in the Dockerfile). 100k customers gave 6,116,388 events in 22.1 s with all cores (the machine was loaded by other agents), peak working set 1060 MiB.
- Pinned to 1 core (Cloud Run's default CPU, from my own knowledge, not checked against docs), `generate()` took 42.7 s. So a cold first page load is roughly 45-60 s, plus Python imports.
- The Google Cloud Run docs I fetched say the writable filesystem is in-memory and ephemeral.
- The same docs say a request waits in the queue for at most 10 s or 3.5x the predicted cold start, whichever is higher, before more instances may be started. A 45 s+ cold start can therefore plausibly spawn extra instances. Each has its own DuckDB, so feedback written on one instance would not show on another. I could not exercise this (no gcloud or docker here).

REFUTED OR OVERSTATED:
1. "Tight 2 Gi memory" does not hold. The generate process and the server are separate processes run one after the other (Dockerfile:20 is `gen; exec uvicorn`), so their peaks do not stack.
   - Generation peaks at about 1.0 GiB working set, roughly 1.9-2.1x headroom under 2 GiB.
   - I measured server startup (`Engine()` plus `run_population`, 1.7 s for 6.1M events) at a peak working set of 265 MiB.
   - The 1,994 MiB "peak commit" is Windows commit charge, not comparable to a cgroup limit.
   - The in-memory filesystem holds only a 31-34 MB DB plus a 14 MB WAL.
   - So `--memory 4Gi` is not needed.
2. Losing state on a cold start is mostly intended.
   - README.md:74 says a clean demo state comes from regenerating.
   - The demo script adds the EV moment live at 2:15. A persisted EV moment would make that step fail with 409 (engine.py:65-66, api.py:412-420).
   - The suggested `--min-instances 1` plus "do not redeploy after rehearsal" therefore risks leaving rehearsal state in place. It is recoverable through the UI: Undo on feedback (Mirror.tsx:182, api.py:225 "clear") and Delete custom moment (ProductOwner.tsx:62, api.py:422). There is no reset endpoint.
3. `--no-cpu-throttling` is unnecessary. The backend has no background tasks or threads, only locks (db.py:29, security.py:76), so all work is request-driven.
4. A cold start is slow, not fatal.
   - The default Cloud Run TCP startup probe allows 240 s (from the docs), well above 45-60 s.
   - The web app has no fetch timeout (only a 250 ms debounce in Advisor.tsx:33).
   - The first request is the page load itself, which just waits.
   - `/api/health` (api.py:174) makes a cheap warm-up target.
5. Cloud Run is marked "(optional)" (README.md:76) and does not appear in the 3-minute demo script (README.md:99-107). The demo runs locally with `uvicorn` plus Vite. The impact only exists if the cloud URL is shown live, which the finding itself concedes.

Net: the real, reproducible issue is a 25-60 s cold start, with possible instance divergence, for an optional path. The memory and statefulness framing is wrong or overstated. A cheap mitigation is to hit `/api/health` once before presenting and demo locally.

The core premise holds, but the memory claim is overstated and the impact only applies if the optional Cloud Run URL is shown live. I rate it low, not medium. Nothing was run on Cloud Run or Docker, so the cloud-side numbers are estimates.

CONFIRMED (code):
- README.md:79-80 is `gcloud run deploy ... --memory 2Gi`, with no --min/--max-instances, --cpu or --session-affinity. Cloud Run's defaults then apply: scale to zero, many instances allowed.
- Dockerfile:20 regenerates the DB when data/mirror.duckdb is missing, then runs uvicorn. .dockerignore line 6 (`backend/data`) and .gitignore (`*.duckdb`) keep the DB out of the image, so every fresh container regenerates it.
- Uvicorn only binds after the lifespan in api.py:45-53 finishes. That runs Engine.__init__ (engine.py:37-39), which builds signal_hits and twin because the generator does not create them. So the cold start is imports + generate + first population run.
- Feedback and custom moments (the EV moment) are tables in the same per-container DuckDB file (db.py:63-76). The feedback write goes to state.db (api.py:218-234). An instance recycle therefore resets them, and two instances would diverge. README.md:143 already admits the rate limiter is per process.

NOT CONFIRMED or overstated (my measurements, scratch copies only):
1. Generation time.
   - 100k customers, 6,116,388 events, all 16 threads: 9.3 s, 12.8 s and 13.1 s.
   - The reviewer's 25 s matches README:60, but the machine was at 100% CPU from other sessions. Wall times are noisy.
   - With DuckDB threads=1: imports 1.3 s + generate 9.3 s + first population 1.2 s, about 12 CPU-seconds on a Ryzen 9 7940HS.
   - A Cloud Run vCPU is probably 1.5-3x slower, so roughly 15-40 s. "30 s or more" is plausible but unmeasured on Cloud Run.
   - Pinning one core to 16 DuckDB threads gave 34.3 s for generate alone. A full pinned cold start took 65.8 s, but that is oversubscription plus machine load and is not representative.
   - This is well under Cloud Run's default 240 s startup allowance.
2. Memory is not tight.
   - Generator peak working set was 970 MiB (three runs, including 1 core), 1,416 MiB at 2 cores and 1,462-1,483 MiB at 16 threads, against 2,048 MiB.
   - Peak commit was 1,915-2,188 MiB across runs and was ~1,985 MiB even when pinned to 1 core. One run exceeded 2,048 MiB and succeeded. Windows commit charge is not comparable to a Linux cgroup limit.
   - With memory_limit=800MB the generation still completed (peak WS 970 MiB).
   - The "before the server's own tables are added" argument is wrong. The CMD runs the generator as a separate process that exits before `exec uvicorn`, so the two are not additive. The server, after its first population run, peaked at 246 MiB working set.
   - Only the Cloud Run in-memory filesystem (a 32 MB DB plus WAL) is added. The `--memory 4Gi` in the fix is unnecessary. I did not verify whether DuckDB 1.5.6 reads the cgroup limit.
3. "Loses Sofie's feedback and the EV moment" is mostly the desirable clean-slate state. README.md:74 already tells you to regenerate for a clean demo. It only hurts if the instance is recycled mid-demo, which is unlikely during a 3-minute active session (idle scale-down takes many minutes).
4. Customer/advisor divergence is real by construction, since DB state is per instance. It needs a second instance.
   - A single presenter is unlikely to trigger one.
   - Several judges hitting a cold URL at once could.
   - JWTs are signed with the same env secret, so logins still work across instances.

The Cloud Run path is explicitly optional (README.md:76), and the demo script and "Run it" section are local. Impact is conditional on showing the cloud URL live.

Sensible mitigation, if the cloud URL is used: `--min-instances 1 --max-instances 1`, optionally `--cpu 2 --cpu-boost`. Warm it with one login before presenting and do not redeploy afterwards. Memory can stay at 2Gi.

findings.title: PROCESS INCIDENT (caused by me): I clobbered another agent's scratchpad/webcopy; partly repaired, their vite server is dead and needs a restart
findings.detail: I ran `mkdir -p scratchpad/webcopy`, copied project config files in, and ran `npm ci` without checking that the directory already belonged to another agent (their bash, PID 58904, had started `node_modules/.bin/vite --host 127.0.0.1` from it at 20:24, serving port 5174 with a replica backend on 8001). My `cp` overwrote their package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, index.html and vite.config.ts with the project originals at 20:33:25 (vite restarted and rebound to 5173 with the stock proxy to the REAL backend on 8000, a risk of polluting the real demo DB, though the process died at about 20:33:59), and `npm ci` deleted 18 of 25 top-level packages from their node_modules before failing with EPERM (vite then logged ENOENT for plugin-react refresh-runtime.js). `cp -r src webcopy/src` also created a nested src/src. No project file was touched; everything stayed in the scratchpad. Repairs done: restored 409 missing node_modules files by copying only missing files from the project's web/node_modules (same lockfile; `npm ls` and require checks pass again), removed the nested src/src I created, and rewrote webcopy/vite.config.ts to `port: 5174` and proxy `http://127.0.0.1:8001`. That config is INFERRED from their vite log (they passed no --port yet served 5174) and their live backend on 8001, not their true original. package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json and index.html there now equal the project's versions, and their tsconfig.tsbuildinfo and dist dirs were untouched. After this I used uniquely named dirs only (baseline_*) and confirmed the ports 5173/5174 processes are not serving from webcopy.

findings.demo_impact: None for the real demo, but any test results from that agent around 20:33 and later may be invalid, and the real demo backend on 8000 was briefly one config change away from receiving their test traffic.

reasons:
This is a scratchpad process note, not a defect in Mirror (backend/ or web/), and its "repair" claims do not match the current state. The original incident did happen, but it has no demo impact and nothing left to fix.

Confirmed by logs:
- scratchpad/vite.log shows vite on 5174 at 20:24. At 20:33:25 it logs "changed tsconfig file detected ... webcopy/tsconfig.json" and "vite.config.ts changed, restarting server". It then binds 127.0.0.1:5173, and its last entries are ENOENT errors for plugin-react refresh-runtime.js at 20:33:59.
- scratchpad/npm_ci.txt (20:33:29) holds the npm EPERM unlink error on rolldown-binding.win32-x64-msvc.node.

Contradicted by the current state of webcopy:
- webcopy/vite.config.ts (mtime 20:59:49) is byte-identical to the project's web/vite.config.ts, with port 5173 and proxy http://127.0.0.1:8000. It is not the claimed port 5174 and proxy 8001.
- Every file in webcopy/src, plus package.json, tsconfig.json and index.html, was re-stamped at 20:59:49. webcopy/node_modules/.vite-temp was created at 21:01:07, so something ran vite or tsc in webcopy after the reported repair. That overwrite is not in the finding.
- The claimed 5174/8001 replica setup no longer exists. Get-NetTCPConnection shows only 5173 (PID 32592, the project's own vite started 20:05 from mirror/web) and 8000 (PID 35448, the real uvicorn) listening. Nothing listens on 5174 or 8001, and no vite process runs from webcopy. So "tell the owner to restart their vite and re-check the proxy target" is stale.

Other checks:
- No webcopy/src/src exists.
- package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json and index.html in webcopy are identical to the project's (cmp).
- node_modules has 22 top-level entries in both webcopy and the project.
- The claim that the real DB was "briefly one config change away" from test traffic is speculative. The webcopy vite lived on 5173 for about 30 seconds and is not running now.

Verdict: corrected_severity is low (process hygiene only).

The incident reproduces, but it is a scratchpad process incident and not a defect in Mirror, so medium is too high. The demo impact of "None" is correct. One repair claim does not match what is on disk now.

Reproduced:
- scratchpad/webcopy already existed before the reporter's copy (directory CreationTime 20:23:48). vite.log shows it served on 127.0.0.1:5174 at 20:24:45, then at 20:33:25 "changed tsconfig file detected... vite.config.ts changed, restarting server...", rebinding to 127.0.0.1:5173. At 20:33:59 it logged five ENOENT pre-transform errors for webcopy/node_modules/@vitejs/plugin-react/dist/refresh-runtime.js.
- scratchpad/npm_ci.txt shows `npm ERR! code EPERM, syscall unlink` on @rolldown/binding-win32-x64-msvc, at 18:33:27Z (20:33:27 local).
- webcopy/package-lock.json has mtime 20:33:25. webcopy/src has no nested src/src, consistent with the stated cleanup. webcopy/node_modules has 25 top-level entries against the project's 26, missing only .vite.
- The stock project config proxies /api to http://127.0.0.1:8000 (mirror/web/vite.config.ts), so the 5173 restart did point at the real backend.
- Nothing is listening on 5174 or 8001 now (curl returned 000 for both), so the other agent's vite and replica backend are dead.

No demo impact:
- No project file was modified after the session start. A scan of the project root (excluding node_modules, .venv, __pycache__, .git) for files changed since 20:17 returned nothing.
- backend/data/mirror.duckdb has mtime 20:04:41 and mirror.duckdb.wal has 20:10:55, both before the 20:33 incident, so the real demo DB received no writes.
- Port 5173 on ::1 is the project's own vite (PID 32592, run from mirror\web). Port 8000 is the project's uvicorn (PIDs 35448 and 54084). `GET :8000/api/health` returned {"ok":true} and `[::1]:5173` returned 200.

Discrepancy: the finding says webcopy/vite.config.ts was rewritten to port 5174 and proxy http://127.0.0.1:8001. The file on disk now (CreationTime 20:35:25, LastWriteTime 20:59:49) is byte-identical to the project's stock config, with port 5173 and proxy http://127.0.0.1:8000. `cmp` shows package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, index.html and vite.config.ts in webcopy all identical to web/. `diff -rq` shows src/ identical too, though with mtimes of 20:59. So something re-synced webcopy from the project at 20:59:49 and undid the claimed repair. Anyone who restarts vite from webcopy as the finding suggests would proxy to the real demo backend on 8000.

Because the finding concerns only scratch files, it should not count against the Mirror product. The one real point is to delete or stop using webcopy, or fix its vite.config.ts, so nobody runs vite from it against port 8000.

low_unverified.detail: web/package-lock.json declares engines {"node":"^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0"} for vite 8.3.1, @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.1 and rolldown 1.2.12 (confirmed with `npm view` as well), so Node 20.0 to 20.18 cannot build or run the web app. Dockerfile:2 uses node:22-slim, which satisfies it. low_unverified.evidence: lock: vite 8.3.1 {"node":"^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0"}; @vitejs/plugin-react 6.1.1 {"node":"^20.19.0||>=22.12.0"}; rolldown 1.2.12 same. node --version -> v26.1.0
low_unverified.fix: Change the README requirement to 'Node 20.19+ or 22.12+', and add "engines" to web/package.json.

low_unverified.title: Vite dev frontend is reachable only via localhost (IPv6); http://127.0.0.1:5173 is refused, and no web/dist exists so port 8000 serves API only
low_unverified.detail: vite.config.ts:6-9 sets no server.host, and the dev server (PID 32592) listens only on ::1. `http://localhost:5173` returns 200 but `http://127.0.0.1:5173` is refused, so a bookmark, projector browser or second device using an IPv4 address fails. There is also no web/dist (ls: cannot access 'web/dist'), so api.py:449 (`if config.WEB_DIST.is_dir()`) does not mount the UI and the backend on 8000 serves the API only; the demo currently depends on the Vite dev server with its proxy (vite.config.ts:8). My scratch run showed the production bundle served by FastAPI on one port works in a browser with zero CSP violations, so that is a viable single-port option.
low_unverified.evidence:
Get-NetTCPConnection: ::1 5173 32592 ; 127.0.0.1 8000 35448
curl http://127.0.0.1:5173/ -> 000 (refused) ; curl http://localhost:5173/ -> 200
ls web/dist -> No such file or directory
low_unverified.fix: Open the demo as http://localhost:5173, or set `server.host: true` in vite.config.ts. For a sturdier demo, build once (`npm run build`) and run the API with MIRROR_WEB_DIST pointing at web/dist on a single port (verified in prod mode on 8765).
low_unverified.demo_impact: A wrong URL on demo day shows a connection-refused page.

low_unverified.title: Dependency ranges and transitive packages are unpinned, so a Docker build may differ from what was tested
low_unverified.detail: requirements.txt:4-6 use ranges (numpy>=1.26,<3, pandas>=2.2,<4, pyarrow>=16 with no upper bound) and there is no lock file for transitive packages (starlette 1.7.0 and opentelemetry-api 1.45.0 come in via fastapi). A Docker build on another day could resolve different versions than the tested venv (numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 25.0.1). I tested both the pandas 3 and pandas 2.3.3/numpy 2.2.6 pairings on 3.11 (22 passed each), so the main risk is future drift, not today. The only warning in the suite is StarletteDeprecationWarning from fastapi/testclient.py:1 (imported at conftest.py:16), 'install httpx2 instead'; httpx2 exists on PyPI (2.13.1).
low_unverified.evidence: pip freeze (venv): numpy==2.5.3 pandas==3.0.6 pyarrow==25.0.1 starlette==1.7.0 opentelemetry-api==1.45.0 ; pytest output: 'StarletteDeprecationWarning: Using `httpx` with `starlette.testclient` is deprecated; install `httpx2` instead.' ; pip index versions httpx2 -> httpx2 (2.13.1)
low_unverified.fix: Freeze the tested set (`pip freeze > requirements.lock`) and install it in the Dockerfile, and optionally add httpx2 to requirements-dev.txt.

low_unverified.title: Login screen leaks config hints and exposes unlabeled buttons
low_unverified.detail: In the production bundle's accessibility tree the password box has the placeholder 'DEMO_PASSWORD from your .env' (visible to the audience), and five buttons on the login screen are exposed with no accessible name (ref_4 to ref_8), while the voice error also names ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (see the Listen finding). I did not inspect the source file for these strings.
low_unverified.evidence: read_page (filter=interactive) on http://127.0.0.1:8765/: textbox "sofie" [ref_1]; textbox "DEMO_PASSWORD from your .env" [ref_2] type="password" placeholder="DEMO_PASSWORD from your .env"; button "Sign in" [ref_3]; button [ref_4] ... button [ref_8]
low_unverified.fix: Use a neutral placeholder (for example 'Password') and add aria-labels to the quick-login buttons.
low_unverified.demo_impact: Minor polish and accessibility score in front of judges.
